summary:
I REBUILT THEIR HARNESS FROM SCRATCH BEFORE BELIEVING ANY NUMBER, and it lands on their baseline
bit-for-bit (aux 0.5134152173995972, composed 4.414819717407227, sum|g|max 1.3968892609970744; and at
step_windows=1, sum|g|max 1.202134904637731). I then drove 129 float cells, 78 int cells, the six counts at 0 and
at 1, every declared zero sentinel, the shipped defaults, and a HEAD-checkout copy of the three files for the
before side -- every cell a fresh subprocess. THE MECHANISM HALF OF THEIR WORK STANDS: 126/129 float cells refused
at fab.build, 3/3 FAB_PRESSURE cells refused inside spine.assemble.build, 78/78 int cells refused by owned name,
all six counts refused at 0 and building at 1, all 43 floats rebuilding at their own default, and every declared
zero sentinel still legal -- FAB_DEPTH0=0, FAB_DOM_FRAC=0, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W=0, FAB_ROUTE_T=0, FAB_HALT_MAX=0,
FAB_ALPHA=0, FAB_CENT_EMA=0, FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0, FAB_DOM_MIN=0 and the seven guard-floored zeros. NO REFUSAL
REFUSES A LEGAL CONFIGURATION: for every one of the six counts, 1 spells what 0 used to do (measured: FAB_HOPS=1
and FAB_SLOTS=1 are BIT-IDENTICAL in aux, composed and sum|g|max to what 0 produced on the HEAD tree), and no FAB
lever declares an infinity as a reading.

FIVE THINGS THEY DID NOT REPORT, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE THE ONES THAT MATTER.

(1) THEIR OWN COMMIT DID THE THING ITS NEW COMMENT SAYS IT AVOIDED. src/fabric/levers.py gained a blank line at
line 110, inside the module docstring, ABOVE all three of the census spans that tests/test_census.py::N8 opens.
Every one of those spans moved down one line. `src/fabric/levers.py:344-352` was cut to END on
`route_learn = Lever(True, ...)`; that declaration is now at line 353 and is OUTSIDE its own departure's span.
296-307 and 155-163 each lost their closing line the same way and now open on a blank line. The new footer
paragraph in that very file says, in as many words: "Adding this block at the top instead moved all three spans off
their arguments and failed that check: measured, not assumed. Appending leaves every span above untouched." It did
not. N8 stays green only because the prose above each declaration still spells the lever name.

(2) THE FAB_PRESSURE REFUSAL'S STATED GROUND IS FALSE, AND THE SENTENCE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Both the docstring and
the refusal say the lever cannot be named because "two couplings reach this function with two different packages'
values (FAB.d_operating_population from FAB_PRESSURE and FAB_SLOTS, CAP.d_operating_population from the same pair
...)" -- "two different packages' values" and "from the same pair" in one sentence. spine/assemble.py:1045 and
:1136 both read `derive.operating_population(r["FAB"].pressure, r["FAB"].slots)`, both declare
`src=("FAB.pressure","FAB.slots")`, and src/capacity/api.py:1060 calls the wire "FAB_PRESSURE x FAB_SLOTS" itself.
There is exactly ONE lever behind all three call sites (the third is fabric/api.py:916). FAB_PRESSURE could have
been named. The refusal fires and is a large improvement on the bare `cannot convert float NaN to integer` -- but
the report's census line "refused BY NAME at nan/inf/-inf 129/129" is wrong by three cells, by their own account of
those three.

(3) A FINITE FAB_BAL_FLOOR REPRODUCES THE -inf HARM BIT-FOR-BIT AND STILL BUILDS. FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-24 at
step_windows=100000 gives aux -0.19620820879936218, composed 3.7051963806152344, sum|g|max 3.8982786779924936 --
digit for digit the -inf cell their finding calls critical and closed -- and renders the identical Gate line
`fab.balance: FIRED (balance=0.01 x warm=-24.0 vs > 0)`. They disclose that a finite negative is unrefused and
quote -0.15; they do not report that a plain finite number reproduces the whole measured harm exactly.

(4) TWO LIVE GATES PRINT PAIRS THEIR OWN VERDICT DOES NOT TEST, AND NEITHER K15 NOR K16 SEES EITHER. fab.balance's
verdict is `balance_w > 0.0` while the pair it prints is the PRODUCT `balance x warm` -- so at any finite negative
bal_floor past bal_warm it prints FIRED beside 0.01 x -0.15, which is not > 0. fab.halt renders the CUMULATIVE
halted mass over `depth` hops against a PER-HOP ceiling: at FAB_HALT_MAX=0.001 it prints
`FIRED (mean halted mass 0.003 vs halt_max=0.001)` -- three times its own printed threshold. Both are pre-existing,
both are reachable at finite legal values today, and both are the exact half K15 (reason text) and K16 (pair-is-a-
clause-of-the-verdict) each leave uncovered.

(5) THE NEW REFUSALS ARE SATISFIED-BY-PROSE UNDER THIS TREE'S OWN READER. Running
tests/test_fabric.py::_names_lever_and_value over the message that refuses FAB_SLOTS=0 returns True for FOUR
lever/value pairs -- (FAB_SLOTS,0), (FAB_SLOTS,12), (FAB_N0,6) and (FAB_RANK,0) -- because the static baseline
sentence attaches values to four lever names. Worse: the message that refuses FAB_CULL_FRAC=inf returns True for
(FAB_CENT_EMA, 0), a lever that was never set to a value that was never typed, while returning False for the lever
it actually refused. That helper's own docstring exists because two older refusals in this tree did a milder
version of this.

Also, smaller and all measured: "FOUR VALUES PER LEVER" is printed five times across the three files, including
inside the operator-facing refusal, for a rule that refuses THREE (nan, +inf, -inf) -- the same sentence enumerates
the three. The `_decay_to_floor` claim that "a full re-grep of this file found no fifth" max site is right on the
count but wrong on the reason: `max(int(dom_min), int(dom_frac * ...))` in _breadth_ban takes a FLOAT lever's value
through an int() conversion, and what protects it is int() raising, not "an int lever cannot hold a nan" -- the
same file records that site raising a bare ValueError at FAB_DOM_FRAC=nan. And the FAB_ALPHA=1e26 pair
(aux 0.5150710, composed 2.943258) quoted four times is a ONE-pass VOCAB-11 sweep measurement sitting in a file
whose other numbers are two-pass; I reproduced it exactly in the sweep's harness and got aux 0.5215709209442139 /
composed 3.9239108562469482 / 15 of 23 in the harness the same paragraphs quote as their baseline. The 15/23 and
the bounding argument hold in both.

(a) fab.balance, src/fabric/api.py::forward. The verdict is `balance_w > 0.0`. The printed pair is the PRODUCT: value=f"balance={balance_w} x warm={round(bal_scale, 4)}", threshold="> 0". bal_scale is _decay_to_floor(step, bal_warm, bal_floor) and goes NEGATIVE at any negative FAB_BAL_FLOOR once step passes bal_warm. MEASURED, after the fix, all legal:
  FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-0.15 step_windows=100000 -> Gate(name='fab.balance', fired=True, value='balance=0.01 x warm=-0.15', threshold='> 0')
  FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-24   step_windows=100000 -> value='balance=0.01 x warm=-24.0', fired=True, threshold='> 0'
A reader doing the arithmetic the line invites gets 0.01 x -24.0 = -0.24, which is not > 0, beside the word FIRED. K16 does not see it because the pair is not one clause of the verdict -- it is the verdict's clause TIMES a factor the verdict never tests; K15 does not see it because there is no reason text on the fired arm.
(b) fab.halt, same function. value = round(float((1.0 - alive).mean()), 4) -- the CUMULATIVE halted mass over `depth` hops, since `alive = alive * (1 - ph)` compounds -- rendered against threshold=f"halt_max={halt_max}", which caps the PER-HOP probability.   FAB_HALT_MAX=0.05 / 0.3 / 0.9 -> value='mean halted mass 0.0139' (the cap does not bind; no contradiction)
1-(1-0.001)^3 = 0.0029970 and 1-(1-0.005)^3 = 0.01493, so the arithmetic is the compounding, not a bug in the mass. `fired` is just `halt_on` (FAB_HALT), so the pair is decorative and reads as a comparison that was never made.
